### Executive Summary
- Multiple **actively exploited zero-days on perimeter/security management platforms** (F5 BIG‑IP APM, Check Point Management Server, VeloCloud Orchestrator) — treat as **edge-compromise risk** and prioritize patch/mitigation + compromise checks.
- **Endpoint escalation/defense-evasion enablers** surfaced (Veeam Agent LPE PoC; “BigDiskBuster” Defender-update DoS PoC) — increase vigilance for post-compromise activity and degraded AV posture.
- **Phishing + supply-chain pressure** continues (M365 inbox compromise service disruption; malicious npm packages/loader) — reinforce email/IdP monitoring and developer dependency controls.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) F5 BIG‑IP APM unauthenticated RCE zero-day (OAuth/Apm-specific)**
- What happened: F5 patched **CVE-2026-94127** in BIG‑IP APM; **active exploitation** reported (unauth RCE) in setups where APM acts as an **OAuth authorization server**.
- Why it matters operationally: Internet-facing IAM/VPN access tier compromise can yield **credential theft/session token abuse**, traffic manipulation, and rapid lateral movement.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Inventory/exposure check** (BIG‑IP with APM+OAuth profile); **urgently patch/apply vendor mitigations** and start **retro-hunt for new admin accounts/config changes and suspicious APM/OAuth traffic**.

**2) Check Point Security Management Server pre-auth script execution zero-day**
- What happened: Check Point released emergency fixes for **CVE-2026-93616**; **active exploitation** allows unauth attackers to upload/execute scripts via management web service exposure.
- Why it matters operationally: Management plane compromise can lead to **policy tampering**, credential harvesting, and pivoting into protected segments (high blast radius in financial networks).
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Confirm hotfix applied** on all Management/Log servers; **restrict management exposure** (no Internet, tight ACLs) and **review management audit logs** for unexpected script execution / file writes.

**3) Arista/VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) critical exploited flaw (on-prem)**
- What happened: Arista reported **active exploitation** of **CVE-2026-93952** (CVSS 10) affecting **on‑prem VCO**, particularly certificate-based setups.
- Why it matters operationally: SD‑WAN orchestration compromise enables **fleet-wide device control**, traffic interception/redirection, and credential/material theft.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Identify any on‑prem VCO** and its auth mode; **patch immediately** and **monitor for anomalous admin/API actions** (new users, cert changes, edge re-provisioning).

**4) Chrome→Windows zero-day chain used by China-nexus actor to drop malware**
- What happened: Reports of a China-linked actor exploiting a **Chrome + Windows zero-day chain** (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491, plus Windows component) via **fake sites** to deploy **CLEANGULP** malware.
- Why it matters operationally: High-likelihood **initial access via web browsing** (drive-by/social engineering), leading to stealthy footholds on user endpoints (trader/ops workstations are prime targets).
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Verify Chrome/Windows patch levels** and push updates; **hunt for browser-spawned suspicious child processes** and unusual outbound from user endpoints shortly after web access events.

**5) Actively exploited / PoC edge + infra weaknesses (Zyxel KEV, WordPress core RCE chain, Veeam Agent LPE PoC)**
- What happened: **Zyxel GS1900 (CVE-2026-7273)** added to KEV; WordPress critical issues/weaponized PoCs circulating; **Veeam Agent for Windows LPE (CVE-2026-32996)** now has PoC and exploitation chatter.
- Why it matters operationally: These enable **rapid opportunistic compromise** (edge devices/web stacks) and **privilege escalation** post-initial access; both are common ransomware playbook steps.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Triage exposure** (Zyxel/WordPress/Veeam footprint); **patch/mitigate where present** and **raise alerting** for exploitation patterns (webshell indicators on WP; local admin escalation on Veeam-protected hosts).

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **F5 / Check Point / VCO (edge management) compromise checks:** collect and review **appliance audit logs, config change logs, admin auth logs, and system command execution logs**; alert on **new admin accounts, policy exports, unexpected script/file writes** (MITRE: T1190, T1556, T1562).
- **Network telemetry around exposed management interfaces:** on **firewalls/WAF/IPS**, alert on spikes to **management ports/URIs**, unusual **POST/PUT uploads**, and repeated 4xx/5xx bursts preceding success (T1190).
- **Endpoint hunting for browser-to-payload behavior (Chrome/Windows chain):** in **EDR**, detect **chrome.exe/msedge.exe spawning cmd/powershell/wscript/rundll32/regsvr32** and new persistence shortly after browsing (T1204, T1059, T1547).
- **Email/IdP monitoring tied to “phishing service” activity:** in **M365 audit logs + IdP sign-ins**, alert on **impossible travel, new OAuth consent grants, mailbox rule creation/forwarding**, and atypical token use (T1566, T1114, T1550).
- **Veeam Agent LPE posture:** in **EDR + Windows Security logs**, watch for **service manipulation**, suspicious binaries executed with SYSTEM, and privilege escalation artifacts on endpoints with Veeam Agent installed (T1068).
- **Defender-update DoS (disk fill) early warning:** monitor **EDR + Windows event logs + disk utilization** for rapid disk consumption on endpoints/servers paired with **Defender update failures** (T1562.001).
- **Supply-chain npm threats:** from **CI/CD logs, proxy logs, EDR on build agents**, alert on **new/rare npm package installs**, postinstall scripts spawning shells, and unexpected outbound from runners (T1195, T1059).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance:** ensure perimeter platforms (F5/Check Point/VCO) are on **emergency patch cadence** with documented **compensating controls** (mgmt plane isolation, MFA, allowlisting).
- **Exposure reduction:** confirm **no Internet exposure** for security management interfaces; enforce **jump-host only** access + strict firewall rules and continuous external attack surface monitoring.
- **Web platform hardening:** validate **WordPress core/plugins** patch SLAs, disable unused plugins, restrict admin access, and implement WAF rules for common WP exploitation chains.
- **Backups/EDR resilience:** review controls against **post-compromise escalation** (Veeam LPE) and **security tooling disruption** (Defender update failures); ensure alternative AV update paths and disk quota monitoring.
- **Developer supply-chain controls:** require **dependency pinning/lockfiles**, provenance verification where possible, and tighten **build agent egress**; consider internal allowlist for npm scopes/packages.
- **Phishing readiness:** refresh playbooks for **token theft/OAuth abuse** in M365 (containment steps: revoke sessions/tokens, disable forwarding rules, app consent review) and run a quick SOC tabletop this week.
